newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finmin sees 1.5-2.0 pct point drop in rates.
newsitem.headline: Thai finmin sees 1.5-2.0 pct point drop in rates.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan on Thursday said he expected Thai interest rates to fall 1.50-2.00 percentage points in 1997.
The minister told reporters the expected Thai rate decline next year would be in line with world market trends.
Amnuay also told a business seminar that Thai business, hurt by zero-growth exports this year, would benefit from lower interest rates and cheaper funding costs.
The minister said he would sustain Thailand's financial liberalisation initiated by previous governments.

Olarn Chaipravat, president of the Thai Bankers Association, also projected a 1.50 percentage point fall in Thai lending rates in 1997 as the U.S. Federal Reserve Board has signalled that it would not raise interest rates for the next six months.
Olarn, also chief executive of the Siam Commercial Bank Plc, said increased market intervention efficiency of the Thai central bank would be conducive to lower Thai lending rates next year.
The banker said Thai money market liquidity would also be boosted in 1997 by a scheduled launch of several new pension funds for state enterprise employees and corporate provident funds next year.
